detail: finding, page 11: The share of Moldovan businesses using digital services is low, which harms productivity and market reach.
metric, page 11: Only 30% of essential business services are online in Moldova, against over 70% in many EU countries.
finding, page 11: Despite good coverage, internet connectivity quality and reliability remain inadequate in some areas.
barrier, page 11: Cybersecurity and data protection concerns deter businesses from adopting digital solutions.
finding, page 14: There is a significant urban-rural digital divide; many rural communities lack infrastructure, limiting internet speed and reliability.
metric, page 14: One third of people aged 60 and over use the internet regularly, against 82% of those aged 15 to 59.
finding, page 14: Moldova's 5G networks are still evolving, though some operators plan substantial investments.
finding, page 14: 5G technology introduces new security challenges, particularly regarding third-party vendors.
finding, page 14: Slow modernisation of digital infrastructure such as fibre and 5G affects connectivity and competitiveness.
recommendation, page 14: Moldovan networks need a thorough security assessment, targeted investment and a robust 5G regulatory framework.
intervention, page 14: Moldova has digitised public services over the past decade through platforms including MCloud, MPass, MPay and MConnect.
metric, page 14: The public services portal gives single sign-on access to 166 e-services.
finding, page 14: The public services portal lacks integration with EU systems, limiting cross-border interactions.
finding, page 14: Digital networks are vulnerable to outages and cyberattacks because of outdated technology and security gaps.
finding, page 14: The cybersecurity framework is still emerging, with some institutions set up only in 2024, leaving the ecosystem exposed.
recommendation, page 14: A framework is needed to identify critical infrastructure operators, manage cyber risks and ensure consistent cybersecurity implementation.
finding, page 14: There are no plans for large-scale cyber incidents, and the 2019-2024 information security strategy lapsed without addressing new threats.
finding, page 40: Some business processes are digitised, but permits, insolvency cases and business registry updates still need paperwork and in-person contact.
intervention, page 47: Moldova will complete accession to the Common Transit Convention and fully implement the NCTS, moving customs to electronic procedures.
intervention, page 59: Secondary legislation will enforce the EU electronic communications acquis, including roaming, termination rates and BEREC rules.
intervention, page 59: The National Agency for Cybersecurity will be legally empowered to conduct audits and will operate from equipped offices.
intervention, page 59: Cybersecurity responsibilities will be clarified and aligned with EU instruments, increasing alignment with the NIS2 Directive.
intervention, page 64: The MTender e-procurement system, launched in 2018, has enabled electronic procurement and public access to documents.
finding, page 64: Because of technical limitations, MTender lacks annual planning and contract management modules, so authorities use alternatives that may cause delays.
finding, page 64: Not all mandated procurement procedures and award instruments are available in MTender, limiting contracting authorities.
intervention, page 64: The electronic procurement system will be re-engineered to promote transparency, equal access and less bureaucracy.
intervention, page 64: Procurement modernisation will include a new electronic system and catalogues, starting with a re-engineering concept for national and European integration.
barrier, page 65: Limited staff and time hamper the State Tax Service in fully digitalising its services.
barrier, page 65: Many taxpayers prefer in-person service to electronic services, slowing modernisation of tax administration.
intervention, page 65: Moldova will digitalise its tax administration and make it interoperable by aligning with EU taxation IT systems.
intervention, page 65: At least two tax services will be digitalised by 2025 and two more in 2026, aiming at 90% service digitalisation.
intervention, page 66: Tax digitalisation will enhance interoperability with EU IT systems and prepare tax infrastructure for European integration.
